newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police identify a victim of bin-bag killer.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police identify a victim of bin-bag killer.

text.p: Police have identified one of the female victims of a serial killer who has terrorised this ancient Belgian town for the past month by leaving parts of up to six bodies scattered about in plastic bin-bags.
But Mons assistant public prosecutor Didier Vanreusel refused at a news conference on Wednesday to confirm newspaper reports that police were holding a suspect in the case.
"The enquiry has allowed the identification of the corpse of one victim. It is a Belgian woman of local origin," Vanreusel said.
"The victim had not previously been signalled as missing. At the request of the family we cannot give the identity," he added.
Police have found 15 bin-bags containing neatly-severed legs, arms, hands, feet, a torso and a head. The head belonged to the victim who has been identified.
Evidence to date indicates the police are dealing with an educated, calculating killer with local historical knowledge, a possible religious bent and a desire to taunt.
Another victim, whose torso was found in a bin bag last year, was a French woman who had worked as a prostitute.
On Tuesday, a court official said it had not been established that the woman, Martine Bohn, was killed by the same murderer who deposited the body parts in the past month.
DNA investigations on the badly decomposed body parts found since March 22 will take several months.

The bags were found in four separate locations around Mons, each with names such as Street of Worry, Deposit Street, River Hate and a street named after Saint Symphorien, a third-century French saint who was decapitated and whose bones are kept as a relic in a nearby church.

"This is clearly the work of a highly intelligent, ritual psychopath, as you can see from the way the body parts are cut, the way they are wrapped and the places in which they are deposited," a police official close to the inquiry told Reuters.

Police are also looking into reports that one of the streets was the site for processions of the Brotherhood of Saint John the Beheaded, a Catholic group which in the Middle Ages accompanied condemned men from their prison to the execution site.
The Brotherhood -- which still exists today and now counsels prisoners -- is named after the biblical John the Baptist, who was decapitated at the request of Salome.
The stone head of Saint John on a plate still adorns a former inn in Mons city centre and there is also a chapel there.
"The places where the bags were deposited indeed have evocative names and this is an important part in our investigation," Vanreusel said.
Investigators also pointed out that the killer must have access to large refrigeration equipment, as he seems to keep the body parts a long time before disposing of them.
Police said they saw no link between the bin-bag serial killer case and the paedophile sex, kidnap and murder scandals that have rocked the country in the past nine months.
